input.quote: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual, but at one month of Fees "actually paid" it is far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and within walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees). The words "without exception" also override the Excluded Claims regime in Section 21.3, placing indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap — a second walk-away trigger. Section 21.2 (consequential damages), 21.3 (Excluded Claims definition and payment-obligation carve-out) and 21.4 (independence/severability) are otherwise consistent with the preferred position, so the minimal fix is to restate 21.1 as the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and delete "without exception" so the existing carve-outs operate.

proposal.summary: Raise cap to greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and remove "without exception" so Excluded Claims stay uncapped
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reset the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, since a one-month cap is well below our minimum. We also deleted "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) sit outside the cap as that Section already contemplates.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
